svg.title: Direct invocation state: one bounded structural change
svg.desc: The baseline wraps a captured continuation in SynchronousSink. The candidate uses a private static DirectInvocation with owner, pipeline, nextIndex and output fields, clearing its three invocation references in finally. Public entry-point and session/async source regions match byte for byte. Source expressions are not physical heap-object counts; guard equivalence also relies on lifecycle tests.

svg.text: Combine the state. Preserve the boundary.
One production file changes; public entry-point and session / async source remains byte-identical.
Pipeline.process → dispatch → processor.process → guarded output → next stage
Detach the owner and downstream delegate.
owner = null / pipeline = null / output = null
A retired handle is never pooled or reactivated.
PRESERVED BEHAVIOR / VERIFIED BY LIFECYCLE FIXTURES
Nested calls, post-output exceptions and retained handles remain part of the correctness boundary.
Checked source boundary: identical public prefix / direct-only edit / identical session and async suffix.
Source expressions do not count physical heap objects; inlining and escape analysis may reshape allocation.
Use paired JMH time and B/op for measured effects. This source check is not a formal equivalence proof.
No sink pooling, session scheduler change, generation-fence change or media-constructor change.
